product_overview: SEC is the platform’s central security module, providing authentication, self-service onboarding and password recovery, plus role-based authorization, auditing, session control, and a live admin dashboard. It also serves as the registry and enforcement layer for module, screen, and action permissions across the ERP platform.
core_goals: Provide secure JWT-based authentication for users and protected APIs
Support self-service sign-up and password reset without exposing sensitive data
Enable administrators to manage users, roles, and hierarchical permissions
Enforce module -> screen -> action grant hierarchy and separation-of-duties constraints
Maintain an immutable audit trail and live operational visibility through dashboard and session controls
Allow consuming modules to register their security metadata without changing SEC code

features.name: Authentication and Self-Service Access
features.description: Allows public sign-up submission, login, and password-reset request/complete flows. Login issues JWT access tokens for all protected SEC endpoints, while password reset remains generic and token-based.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/sec/auth/login with valid credentials -> Receive 200 with accessToken, tokenType, and expiresIn -> Use Authorization: Bearer <accessToken> for protected endpoints
POST /api/v1/sec/auth/login with invalid credentials -> Receive 401 SEC-401-INVALID-CREDENTIALS -> No session is created
POST /api/v1/sec/auth/signup with email and bilingual full names -> Receive 200/201 with SignupRequest status PENDING -> No User is created yet
POST /api/v1/sec/auth/signup with an email that already exists or is pending -> Receive 409 SEC-409-SIGNUP-DUP -> No duplicate request is created
POST /api/v1/sec/auth/password-reset/request with an email -> Receive 200 generic confirmation regardless of email existence -> PasswordResetToken is created if the email matches a user
POST /api/v1/sec/auth/password-reset/complete with a valid token and new password -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Password is updated and token is marked used
POST /api/v1/sec/auth/password-reset/complete with an expired or already-used token -> Receive 409 SEC-409-RESET-TOKEN-INVALID -> Password remains unchanged

features.name: User Administration
features.description: Lets security administrators create, update, deactivate, and reactivate users, plus assign roles to users. Deactivation terminates active sessions immediately.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/sec/users with unique username, email, names, and password -> Receive 200 with created UserResponse -> User status defaults to ACTIVE
POST /api/v1/sec/users with duplicate username or email -> Receive 409 SEC-409-USER-DUP -> No user is created
POST /api/v1/sec/users/search with filters for username, email, name, or status -> Receive 200 with a paginated list of matching users -> Results reflect the requested sort and pagination
PUT /api/v1/sec/users/{id} with updated user fields -> Receive 200 with updated UserResponse -> Changes are persisted
PUT /api/v1/sec/users/{id}/roles with one or more roleIds -> Receive 200 with one assignment row per selected role -> User receives the effective union of those roles
PUT /api/v1/sec/users/{id}/roles with conflicting roles that would violate SoD -> Receive 409 SEC-409-SOD-CONFLICT -> Role assignment is rejected
DELETE /api/v1/sec/users/{id} for an active user -> Receive 200 with statusCode=DISABLED -> Active sessions are terminated and future login fails
PATCH /api/v1/sec/users/{id} for a disabled user -> Receive 200 with statusCode=ACTIVE -> User can authenticate again with valid credentials

features.name: Sign-up Request Review
features.description: Allows administrators to approve or reject pending sign-up requests. Approval creates the user account; rejection closes the request without creating a user.
user_flows: PATCH /api/v1/sec/signup-requests/{id} with decision=APPROVE for a pending request -> Receive 200 with UserResponse -> SignupRequest becomes APPROVED and a new ACTIVE User is created
PATCH /api/v1/sec/signup-requests/{id} with decision=REJECT for a pending request -> Receive 200 with SignupRequestResponse -> SignupRequest becomes REJECTED and no User is created
PATCH /api/v1/sec/signup-requests/{id} for a request that is not PENDING -> Receive 409 SEC-409-INVALID-TRANSITION -> Decision is rejected
PATCH /api/v1/sec/signup-requests/{id} for a missing request id -> Receive 404 SEC-404-SIGNUP -> No state changes occur

features.name: Role and Permission Management
features.description: Supports role creation and hierarchical grant management across modules, screens, and actions. It enforces module-first and screen-first rules, VIEW-before-other-actions, cascading revokes, and SoD checks where applicable.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/sec/roles with role code and names -> Receive 200 with RoleResponse -> Role is created
POST /api/v1/sec/roles with a duplicate role code -> Receive 409 SEC-409-ROLE-DUP -> No duplicate role is created
POST /api/v1/sec/roles/search with paging and filters -> Receive 200 with paginated roles -> Matching roles are returned
POST /api/v1/sec/roles/{id}/modules with a valid moduleId -> Receive 200 with RoleModuleGrantResponse -> Module grant is recorded
DELETE /api/v1/sec/roles/{id}/modules/{moduleId} -> Receive 200 with revoked screen/action counts -> Dependent screen and action grants are cascaded away
POST /api/v1/sec/roles/{id}/screens without an existing module grant -> Receive 409 SEC-409-NO-MODULE-GRANT -> Screen grant is not created
POST /api/v1/sec/roles/{id}/actions without an existing screen grant -> Receive 409 SEC-409-NO-SCREEN-GRANT -> Action grant is not created
POST /api/v1/sec/roles/{id}/actions for CREATE/UPDATE/DELETE without VIEW on the same screen -> Receive 409 SEC-409-NO-VIEW-GRANT -> Non-VIEW action is rejected
POST /api/v1/sec/roles/{id}/actions that would create an SoD conflict -> Receive 409 SEC-409-SOD-CONFLICT -> Conflicting grant is rejected

features.name: Module Registry for Consuming Modules
features.description: Lets platform modules register themselves, their screens, and their actions as data so authorization can evolve without changing SEC code. The registry also supports search and guards against invalid module/screen relationships.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/sec/registry/modules with code and bilingual names -> Receive 200 with ModuleRegistryResponse -> Module becomes registered and active
POST /api/v1/sec/registry/modules with an already registered code -> Receive 409 SEC-409-MODULE-DUP -> No duplicate module is added
POST /api/v1/sec/registry/screens with a registered moduleCode, pageCode, and names -> Receive 200 with ScreenRegistryResponse -> Screen is registered under the module
POST /api/v1/sec/registry/screens with an unregistered moduleCode -> Receive 409 SEC-409-MODULE-NOT-REGISTERED -> Screen is not created
POST /api/v1/sec/registry/actions with a registered pageCode and actionCode -> Receive 200 with ActionRegistryResponse -> Permission code is derived automatically
POST /api/v1/sec/registry/actions with an unregistered pageCode -> Receive 409 SEC-409-SCREEN-NOT-REGISTERED -> Action is not created
POST /api/v1/sec/registry/search with filters -> Receive 200 with paginated registry rows -> Modules, screens, and actions are returned

features.name: Dynamic Menu and Effective Access
features.description: Returns the caller’s effective navigation menu based strictly on granted modules and screens. Ungranted items are omitted, and direct access remains blocked even if the menu hides the destination.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/sec/menu with a bearer token -> Receive 200 with effective module-to-screen tree -> Only granted modules and screens appear
GET /api/v1/sec/menu for a user without a specific module grant -> Receive 200 with that module omitted -> The user never sees inaccessible navigation
GET /api/v1/sec/menu for a user whose roles grant exactly one module and two screens -> Receive 200 with only those items -> The response reflects the effective union of grants
Directly call a protected non-SEC module endpoint without the required module grant -> Receive 403 forbidden from the security interceptor -> Access is denied regardless of menu visibility

features.name: Security Dashboard
features.description: Provides a live-computed administrative dashboard with recent activity, roles/permissions summaries, onboarding funnel metrics, and optional active-session widgets depending on the caller’s permissions.
user_flows: GET /api/v1/sec/dashboard with an authorized admin token -> Receive 200 with live dashboard widgets -> Figures are computed from current data
GET /api/v1/sec/dashboard twice with a new security event between requests -> Receive 200 both times -> Second response reflects the new data without stale caching
GET /api/v1/sec/dashboard with a role lacking the active-sessions permission -> Receive 200 with that widget omitted -> Unauthorized widgets are hidden
GET /api/v1/sec/dashboard without authorization -> Receive a protected-endpoint failure -> Dashboard data is not returned

features.name: Audit Log Search and Export
features.description: Exposes an immutable, searchable security audit trail and a CSV export of filtered entries. Audit records are append-only and cannot be edited through any API.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/sec/audit-log/search with event type and date-range filters -> Receive 200 with matching AuditLogEntryResponse rows -> Returned rows match stored values exactly
GET /api/v1/sec/audit-log/export with the same filters -> Receive 200 text/csv -> Exported rows match the filtered set
POST /api/v1/sec/audit-log/search with filters that match no rows -> Receive 200 with an empty page -> No audit data is altered
Attempt to update or delete an audit entry through the API -> Receive no valid route / failure -> Audit records remain immutable

features.name: Active Session Management
features.description: Lets administrators list live sessions and force-terminate a session when needed. Termination immediately invalidates the session token.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/sec/sessions/search with pagination and filters -> Receive 200 with only non-terminated sessions -> Active sessions are listed with user and activity data
DELETE /api/v1/sec/sessions/{id} for an active session -> Receive 200 with terminatedAt and terminatedBy set -> The token is no longer accepted
DELETE /api/v1/sec/sessions/{id} for a missing session -> Receive 404 SEC-404-SESSION -> No session state changes occur
DELETE /api/v1/sec/sessions/{id} for an already terminated session -> Receive 409 SEC-409-ALREADY-TERMINATED -> Session remains terminated

features.name: Cross-Module User Directory Access
features.description: Provides read-only cross-module access to user contact details and permission holders through the exposed SecUserDirectoryApi surface. This is consumed in-process by other modules, not through HTTP.
user_flows: In-process call to SecUserDirectoryApi.findContact(userPk) for an active user -> Receive a contact object with email, both display names, and active=true -> No password hash, roles, grants, or session data are exposed
In-process call to SecUserDirectoryApi.findContact(userPk) for a disabled user -> Receive the same contact shape with active=false -> Sensitive fields remain hidden
In-process call to SecUserDirectoryApi.findContact(userPk) for an unknown id -> Receive an empty result -> No error is thrown
In-process call to SecUserDirectoryApi.findUserIdsHoldingPermission(permissionCode) for a held permission -> Receive a distinct list of user ids -> Only active-role holders are included
In-process call to SecUserDirectoryApi.findUserIdsHoldingPermission(permissionCode) for an unheld permission -> Receive an empty list -> No user metadata is returned

features.name: Common Configuration, File Categories, and File Storage
features.description: Provides authenticated CRUD-style management for common configurations, file categories, and file metadata, including file upload, access-token issuance for downloads, and unauthenticated token-based download access.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/common/configurations with a key/value payload -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Configuration entry is created
GET /api/v1/common/configurations/{key} with a bearer token -> Receive 200 with the configuration entry -> The value is returned
PUT /api/v1/common/configurations/{key} with updated data -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Configuration is updated
DELETE /api/v1/common/configurations/{key} -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Configuration is deactivated
POST /api/v1/files/categories with category data -> Receive 200 confirmation -> File category is created
POST /api/v1/files/categories/search with filters -> Receive 200 with paginated categories -> Matching categories are returned
GET /api/v1/files/categories/{id} with a bearer token -> Receive 200 with category details -> The category is returned
POST /api/v1/files with multipart file and metadata -> Receive 200 confirmation -> File metadata and content are stored
POST /api/v1/files/{id}/access-token -> Receive 200 with a download access token -> The token can be used for download
GET /api/v1/files/download with a valid access token -> Receive the file content -> No authentication header is required
DELETE /api/v1/files/{id} -> Receive 200 confirmation -> File is deleted
GET /api/v1/files/lookups/{lookupKey} -> Receive 200 with lookup values -> Related lookup data is returned

features.name: Notifications, Templates, Channels, and Logs
features.description: Provides authenticated notification dispatch, channel management, template management, log search, and lookup retrieval for the notification subsystem.
user_flows: POST /api/v1/notifications/dispatch with a valid dispatch payload -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Notification is queued or sent
POST /api/v1/notifications/channels with channel data -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Notification channel is created
POST /api/v1/notifications/channels/search with filters -> Receive 200 with paginated channels -> Matching channels are returned
GET /api/v1/notifications/channels/{id} -> Receive 200 with channel details -> The channel is returned
PUT /api/v1/notifications/channels/{id} with updates -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Channel is updated
DELETE /api/v1/notifications/channels/{id} -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Channel is deactivated
POST /api/v1/notifications/templates with template data -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Template is created
POST /api/v1/notifications/templates/search with filters -> Receive 200 with paginated templates -> Matching templates are returned
GET /api/v1/notifications/templates/{id} -> Receive 200 with template details -> The template is returned
PUT /api/v1/notifications/templates/{id} with updates -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Template is updated
DELETE /api/v1/notifications/templates/{id} -> Receive 200 confirmation -> Template is deactivated
POST /api/v1/notifications/logs/search with filters -> Receive 200 with paginated logs -> Matching notification logs are returned
GET /api/v1/notifications/logs/{id} -> Receive 200 with log details -> The log is returned
GET /api/v1/notifications/lookups/{lookupKey} -> Receive 200 with lookup values -> Related notification lookup data is returned

tech_stack: Spring Security (stateless JWT — no HTTP Basic)

features.name: SEC Authentication
features.description: Login, self-service sign-up submission, and password-reset request/complete. The only public (pre-authentication) SEC endpoints — every other SEC endpoint requires Authorization Bearer <accessToken>. To authenticate for protected endpoints, POST {username, password} to /api/v1/sec/auth/login and read data.accessToken.

endpoints.description: Login with username/password, returns JWT access token
Submit a sign-up request (does not create a User; creates a PENDING SignupRequest)

response_schema.409: SEC-409-SIGNUP-DUP — email already registered or pending

endpoints.description: Request a password reset token by email (generic response whether or not the email exists)

response_schema.200: ApiResponse<ConfirmationResponse> — generic confirmation, same shape regardless of email existence

endpoints.description: Complete a password reset using a token

response_schema.409: SEC-409-RESET-TOKEN-INVALID — token expired or already used

features.name: SEC Users
features.description: Create, update, deactivate/reactivate users; assign roles to a user. All require a bearer token.

endpoints.description: Create a user directly (statusCode defaults ACTIVE)
Search users, paginated (filters on username, email, fullName, statusCode)
Update a user
Assign one or more roles to a user (replaces the set); rejects SoD conflicts

response_schema.200: ApiResponse<UserResponse> — one UserRoleAssignment row per selected role
response_schema.409: SEC-409-SOD-CONFLICT — user would hold two conflicting actions

endpoints.description: Deactivate a user (statusCode=DISABLED) and terminate its active sessions
Reactivate a disabled user (statusCode=ACTIVE)

features.name: SEC Sign-up Requests
features.description: Approve or reject a pending sign-up request; approval creates the User.

endpoints.description: Decide a pending sign-up request (APPROVE creates a User statusCode=ACTIVE and sets SignupRequest APPROVED; REJECT sets it REJECTED, no User created)

features.name: SEC Roles
features.description: Create roles and search them.

endpoints.description: Create a role
Search roles, paginated

features.name: SEC Role Grants
features.description: Grant/revoke module, screen, and action permissions on a role. Enforces cascading rule hierarchy (module -> screen -> action -> VIEW-before-other-actions) and cascade-revoke.

endpoints.description: Grant a module to a role
Revoke a module grant from a role — cascades to delete every dependent screen/action grant under that module
Grant a screen to a role — requires the role already holds the screen's module grant

response_schema.409: SEC-409-NO-MODULE-GRANT — no module grant yet / SEC-409-GRANT-DUP

endpoints.description: Grant an action to a role — requires the screen grant already exists; VIEW must be granted before any other action on that screen; rejects separation-of-duties conflicts

features.name: SEC Module Registry
features.description: Register modules/screens/actions into the permission catalog, and search the registry.

endpoints.description: Register a new module

Register an action under a registered screen (permissionCode derived as PERM_<pageCode>_<actionCode>)
Search the module/screen/action registry, paginated

features.description: Effective navigation menu for the caller, scoped to their own granted modules/screens.

endpoints.description: Get the effective menu for the caller (self-scoped — no input; ungranted modules/screens never appear)

features.name: SEC Security Dashboard
features.description: Administrative dashboard with live-computed figures (recent activity, roles/permissions summary, onboarding funnel); widgets the caller lacks permission for are omitted.

endpoints.description: Get the security dashboard summary, computed live (no caching)

response_schema.200: ApiResponse<DashboardResponse> — recentActivity (last 10 AuditLogEntry), rolesPermissionsSummary.privilegedRoleCount, onboardingFunnel.stalledCount, activeSessions widget (omitted if caller lacks PERM_SEC_SESSIONS_VIEW)

features.name: SEC Audit Log
features.description: Immutable audit trail of security events; searchable and exportable, never editable (no update/delete route exists).

endpoints.description: Search the audit log by eventTypeCode/date range, paginated
Export the audit log matching the given filters as CSV

response_schema.200: text/csv — rows exactly match the filtered set's fields

known_limitations.issue: TC-SEC-034/TC-SEC-035 exercise an in-process cross-module Spring interface (com.erp.sec.crossmodule.SecUserDirectoryApi), not an HTTP endpoint — not reachable via black-box API testing.
known_limitations.impact: These two governed test cases cannot be exercised by an HTTP-based test tool; they require an in-JVM caller.

known_limitations.issue: REQ-SEC-020 separation-of-duties conflicting-action pairs are declared empty in SEC v1 (deferred — see governance/modules/SEC/execution-state.json api_doc_gaps)
known_limitations.impact: SEC-409-SOD-CONFLICT (TC-SEC-020) cannot be triggered through SEC alone without a FIN-owned conflicting pair seeded; use the FIN entry-creator / period-close-approver pair if FIN is seeded, otherwise this scenario cannot be exercised end-to-end in SEC-only test data.

known_limitations.issue: Prior run (2026-09-11, invalidated) hit stale compiled classes under a live JVM, causing every /api/v1/sec/auth/* call to return a bare 500 INTERNAL_ERROR. The app has since been rebuilt and restarted fresh; login now returns 200 with a valid JWT and signup returns 201.
known_limitations.location: N/A — environmental, not a code defect
known_limitations.impact: None on current run; noted for context only.
